newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-STUTTGART REGAIN INITIATIVE IN GERMAN TITLE RACE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-STUTTGART REGAIN INITIATIVE IN GERMAN TITLE RACE.

text.p: VfB Stuttgart regained the initiative in the German championship race when they dislodged Bayern Munich from the top of the table with a 3-1 home victory over Bochum on Saturday.
Stuttgart, who last won the title in 1992 but have struggled to make an impact in recent seasons, took a one point lead over Bayern who slipped to third after a goalless draw at struggling Freiburg.

Stuttgart clinched victory with first-half goals from Brazilian striker Giovane Elber and midfielders Matthias Hagner and Gerhard Poschner, to move level on points with second-placed Bayer Leverkusen, 2-0 winners at Hamburg.

Former German international striker Ulf Kirsten scored Leverkusen's goals in the 52nd and 82nd minutes. Hamburg will need to lift themeselves before a tough UEFA Cup third round, first leg in Monaco on Tuesday.
Reigning champions Borussia Dortmund lost ground after a disappointing 1-1 draw at home to Karlsruhe which kept them in fourth place three points behind the leaders.

Dortmund were able to welcome back international striker Karlheinz Riedle after an 11-week injury layoff and Germany's Euro 96 libero Matthias Sammer came on as a second-half substitute for his first game in eight weeks.

But Dortmund failed to turn their pressure into goals. Sean Dundee gave the visitors a shock lead in the 25th minute after he pounced to score at a corner when Dortmund defender Juergen Kohler failed to clear.
Midfielder Knut Reinhardt struck Dortmund's vital equaliser just before halftime with a long-range free kick that took a deflection off the wall.
"I'm disappointed with the result. In the first half we missed our chances to take a clear lead," Dortmund coach Ottmar Hitzfeld said.

Karlsruhe can now head towards their UEFA Cup third round clash at Denmark's Brondby with extra confidence. Germany's other UEFA Cup campaigners Schalke, who travel to Belgium's Club Brugge on Tuesday, won 3-1 at Fortuna Duesseldorf.
The day also saw a rare victory for promoted Arminia Bielefeld who moved off the bottom of the table with a 3-1 win at 1860 Munich, only their third triumph of the season.
